scope: Pending/claimed pre-execution NFC input drains overlapping FIFO traffic without replacing the original frame or PKE append. Four local-FIFO hunks per parent reviewed; mixed turn/execution hunk57 remains unreviewed.
mapping: Ordinal53 obtains FIFO length into local state; original mailbox length is retained until a new frame is admitted.

Ordinals54/55 validate nonzero FIFO length and32-byte hardware maximum independently of protocol decoding. Bounded1/2-byte late frames are drained when an original input owns the reply turn; unsolicited malformed frames still fail decode.
Ordinal56 reads the FIFO into a local32-byte window, then copies only admitted frames into the mailbox. Read failure revokes the old request and enters RF recovery.

The before-Core portion of ordinal57 is now reflected by Io::interrupt; Io::take does not release the turn while main-loop Request::append writes to PKE. Executing WTX/cancellation admission differs and is not approved by this partial mapping.
Event::Ignored releases its RF turn under the same generation lock; it never resets Core selection, authorization or response source.
remaining: Hunk57 includes admission during live Core execution: Rust retains its existing dedicated WTX/cancellation policy; no C/Rust execution parity is claimed. WTX cache/echo and arbitrary IRQ/endpoint schedules remain open.
Mixed hunk19, physical RF/WTX, CIU stack/PKE, Linux sanitizer acceptance and full source audit remain open.
